A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAPO research, with matching authors, method, and original experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the new Appendices K–M in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM reinforcement-learning experiments, including benchmark accuracy, optimization diagnostics, computational costs, and optimizer, clipping, and regularization analyses in Section 6 and Appendices H–I.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds curvature–KL correlations, policy-divergence trajectories, and accepted-token efficiency analyses in Appendices L–M.

M1.justification: The last-layer curvature model, optimizer representation, token-selection constraints, and policy-update procedure remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1. The new appendices analyze and explain the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and evaluate the same eight reasoning benchmarks described in Section 6. Appendices L–M add diagnostics within the retained setting, without adding datasets, tasks, populations, or input conditions.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain conservative and aggressive GRPO, Dr.GRPO, and REINFORCE, together with the existing curvature-aware extensions. Figure 10 uses the existing comparator set. Appendix M discusses TRPO conceptually but does not evaluate it as a new baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix L adds evaluation against Monte Carlo estimates of between-update KL divergence, with token-level and global Spearman correlations. Appendix M supplements completion-based sample efficiency with accuracy versus accepted tokens. The original training budgets, model, hyperparameters, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 and Figure 9 add targeted validation of whether curvature estimates track actual policy shifts. Figure 10 checks whether sample-efficiency findings persist under accepted-token accounting. The existing optimizer ablation and clipping and KL-regularization analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 5 introduces Spearman correlation estimation as a new statistical association analysis. Appendix G retains the same five-seed, standard-error reporting policy; v2 does not report increased run counts or uncertainty intervals for the new correlations.

E6.justification: The original benchmark curves and reported 30-fold MATH and ninefold TEST sample-efficiency gains are unchanged. New Table 5 reports token/global correlations of 0.622/0.596 for GRPO and 0.459/0.498 for CAPO. Figure 9 reports smoother estimated KL shifts for CAPO, and Figure 10 reports similar efficiency trends when counting accepted tokens.

T1.justification: New Appendix K extends the discounted analysis to the undiscounted finite-horizon setting. It supplies performance-difference, state-distribution-shift, and surrogate-performance-gap lemmas with proofs, derives a finite horizon-dependent bound, and applies it to the monotonic-improvement argument. This substantially expands the theoretical coverage while retaining the earlier derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same curvature-model and masking contributions, stability claims, and up-to-30-fold efficiency claim. The introduction now explicitly identifies standard-regime GRPO as the efficiency comparator, which was already specified elsewhere in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix L argues that monotonic association with policy shifts can suffice without numerical calibration and interprets the KL trajectories as approximate trust-region behavior. Appendix M adds an interpretation concerning token accounting and inference cost. Section 7 retains the existing limitations concerning experimental scale and threshold tuning.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, hardware and runtime disclosures, code location, and planned experiment-log release remain unchanged. The new analyses describe evaluation procedures without adding concrete implementation settings or changing resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Amari et al. (1995) and Amari (1998). Appendix M expands CAPO’s relationship to natural gradients and TRPO, emphasizing shared motivation, CAPO’s Hessian information, and differing memory and computational requirements. The original related-work discussion is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 preserves the original narrative and appendix ordering while appending K–M, including a question-and-answer discussion. Existing prose receives limited clarification, alongside conference-header and funding-acknowledgment additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and Figures 9–10; Figure 10 presents accuracy using an accepted-token horizontal axis. Existing plots and tables retain their contents, while Figures 7–8 receive captions explicitly identifying GRPO. Conference headers and limited text reflow also change the layout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Appendix K improves the relevance of the theory to undiscounted finite-horizon LLM training, and Appendices L–M provide useful checks of the curvature proxy and token accounting. These strengthen support for the existing argument. The gains remain bounded because the acknowledged gap between the true-shift guarantee and the implemented approximate proxy remains; the new correlations do not establish a strict guarantee for that implementation.
